v.rationale:
All three implementations pass their own suites (11 tests each) and my probes: --days=0 with a frozen clock, a huge --days value, an empty --days value, '+7', and a boundary test while time moves. None has a real functional bug in the counting logic. Code quality decides the ranking.

impl-1 is the tightest. It validates with a single filter_var using min_range and then calls $this->fail(); I confirmed that API in Laravel 13.40. Its scope takes the cutoff as a parameter, and its schedule test checks both the cron expression and the log file path. Its test set is the broadest, including an exact-boundary test with freezeTime. Minor issues: the scope type-hints a concrete Carbon class, some output assertions are loose, and the factory state adds a little ceremony.

impl-2 is nearly as good. It has exact output assertions and freezeTime in beforeEach. It loses points for adding withoutOverlapping(10) to a trivial read-only count on a single server, for a manual error-then-return instead of fail(), and for a schedule test that doesn't check the log destination, which was the point of the schedule.

impl-3 is the weakest. It uses a full Validator for one integer option, prints the ungrammatical '1 users', leaves the stale commented line in Pest.php and unsorted imports in User.php, and has a weak assertion for invalid input. It also has no freezeTime, no boundary test and no test for the column.
